sub: Named after at-taghābun, “the Day of loss and gain”, in ayah 9
theme: A call to faith and obedience. It reminds all people who made them, warns the deniers with ruined nations and the Day of loss and gain, then guides believers through hardship, family and giving.
story: Most count it as Madinan; one report says ayat 1–13 came in Makkah and 14–18 in Madinah. Its opening speaks to all people, ayat 5–10 to those who deny, and ayat 11–18 to those who believe.

No single incident lies behind the whole surah. The best-known report is about ayah 14: men who became Muslim in Makkah wanted to emigrate to the Prophet ﷺ, but their wives and children held them back.

When they finally arrived and saw how much others had learned, they wanted to punish their families. Allah told them to pardon and forgive instead. Another report links the ayah to ʿAwf ibn Mālik, whose family pleaded with him not to go on campaign.

sections.title: Everything glorifies Allah, who created and shaped you and knows your hearts
sections.meaning: Everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Allah. He owns all, deserves all praise, and can do anything. He created you; then some disbelieve and some believe, and He sees what each does. He made everything with purpose, shaped you beautifully, and knows your secrets and your hidden thoughts.
points: Everything glorifies Allah: His is the dominion and the praise
He created you; some disbelieve, some believe; He sees all
Created with truth, shaped you well; the return is to Him
He knows the open, the hidden, and what is in hearts
sections.matters: Before any warning or command, the surah lays the foundation: the universe has a Creator, it was made with purpose, your choice between faith and disbelief matters, and you will return to the One who knows even your thoughts.
sections.story: No specific incident. These opening ayat speak to all people. It is the last of the surahs that open with Allah’s glorification (tasbīḥ).
explained: Everything in the heavens and earth declares Allah free of every flaw. All mulk is His, all ḥamd is His, and nothing He wills can be resisted. He created you, and then some became disbelievers and some believers. That happens by His decree, through the will He gave people, and He sees what each one does.

He created the heavens and earth bil-ḥaqq, with wisdom and purpose. He shaped you and made your form the finest of any creature, no two faces alike. You will return to Him and be repaid. He knows what you hide, what you show, and every intention in the heart.
teaches: The whole universe glorifies Allah; join it.
Your choice of faith matters, and Allah sees it.
Your fine form is a gift that calls for thanks.
Guard your inner self: Allah knows every intention.
sections.hook: The surah opens with yusabbiḥu on page 556. Ayat 2 and 3 both say He created (khalaqakum, khalaqa). Ayah 4 says “He knows” (yaʿlamu) twice, then ends with ʿalīm.

sections.title: Past deniers were ruined; resurrection comes, the Day of loss and gain
sections.meaning: Past nations rejected their messengers, saying, “Shall mere humans guide us?” They were ruined here and face punishment hereafter. Today’s deniers say there is no resurrection; the Prophet ﷺ swears they will be raised and told what they did. So believe, before the Day of Gathering: the Day of loss and gain.
points: Past nations rejected human messengers and were ruined
“Yes, by my Lord, you will be resurrected”
So believe in Allah, His Messenger and the light, the Qur’an
The Day of loss and gain: believers win gardens forever
Those who deny Our signs: the Fire forever
sections.matters: It names the two roots of every ruined nation: rejecting the messengers and denying the Hereafter. Then it shows the real scoreboard. Winning and losing in this world mean little; true gain and loss are revealed on the Day of at-taghābun.
sections.story: No specific incident for the section. Ayah 7 was reportedly revealed about al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil of Makkah, in his dealings with Khabbāb, and then applied to every denier.
explained: Haven’t you heard of those who disbelieved before, like ʿĀd and Thamūd? They tasted the bad result in this world, and a painful punishment waits in the next. Their messengers brought clear proofs, but they sneered, “Shall humans guide us?” They turned away, and Allah had no need of them. He is ghanī, free of need, and ḥamīd, praised.

The deniers claim they won’t be raised. The Prophet ﷺ swears, “Yes, by my Lord,” and it is easy for Allah. So believe in the Qur’an, the light. On the Day of Gathering, believers take the places in Paradise the disbelievers lost. The disbeliever’s loss is total, and even a believer regrets the good he missed.
teaches: Rejecting truth because of who brings it is arrogance.
Bringing us back is easy for the One who made us.
The Qur’an is light: follow it.
Real winning and losing happen on the Day of Judgement.
sections.hook: Ayah 7 is one of three places the Prophet ﷺ is told to swear “Yes, by my Lord” (also 10:53, 34:3). Ayat 9 and 10 pair gardens with Fire, both khālidīna fīhā.

sections.title: Every hardship is by Allah’s leave; obey the Messenger, rely on Allah
sections.meaning: No hardship strikes except by Allah’s permission, and whoever believes that, Allah guides his heart. Obey Allah and His Messenger; if you turn away, the Messenger’s only duty was to deliver clearly. There is no god but Allah, so let the believers rely on Him.
points: No calamity except by Allah’s leave; faith guides the heart
Obey Allah and the Messenger; his duty is clear delivery
No god but Allah; believers rely on Him alone
sections.matters: The second ruku turns to the believers. Hardship is where faith is tested. Knowing that everything comes by Allah’s decree turns panic into calm, and the next steps follow: obedience in action, and trust in Allah alone rather than in your own strength.
sections.story: No specific incident is agreed. Reportedly, ayah 11 answered disbelievers who said, “If the Muslims were right, Allah would have protected them from hardship.”
explained: Every muṣībah, in body, wealth or family, comes only by Allah’s idhn: His decree and will. The believer who accepts that is given a guided heart. He stays calm and patient, certain that what hit him was never going to miss him, and what missed him was never going to hit him.

Faith is not only words. Obey Allah and the Messenger. If you turn away, the loss is yours: the Messenger’s job was al-balāgh al-mubīn, delivering clearly. Allah alone deserves worship, so rely on Him in everything. The stronger the faith, the stronger the tawakkul.
teaches: Nothing reaches you except by Allah’s permission.
Accepting Allah’s decree brings calm to the heart.
For a believer, hardship brings patience and blessing brings thanks; both are good.
Faith means obeying, not only believing.
Trust Allah more than your own strength.
sections.hook: The second ruku starts at ayah 11, which repeats “wa man yuʾmin billāh” from ayah 9. Ayah 12 says “obey” (aṭīʿū) twice, and ayah 13 ends with al-muʾminūn.

sections.title: Forgive family who hold you back; spend, a goodly loan Allah multiplies
sections.meaning: Some spouses and children act as enemies by holding you back from Allah: beware, yet pardon and forgive. Wealth and children are a test; Allah’s reward is greater. Fear Allah as much as you can, obey and spend. Whoever is saved from his own stinginess succeeds, and a goodly loan to Allah is multiplied.
points: Some spouses and children are enemies; beware, yet forgive
Wealth and children are a test; Allah’s reward is greater
Fear Allah as much as you can; spend; beat stinginess
A goodly loan multiplied; the Appreciative, Forbearing, Wise
sections.matters: The strongest pull away from Allah is often love, not hatred: love of family and wealth. This section teaches balance. Stay alert but stay kind, obey within your ability, and treat giving as a loan Allah repays many times over.
sections.story: Reportedly about men in Makkah whose wives and children stopped them emigrating. Once in Madinah, they wanted to punish their families, and “if you pardon” was revealed. Another report names ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Ashjaʿī, whose family pleaded with him not to go on campaign.
explained: Min azwājikum: among your spouses and children, not all of them. They become enemies by what they do: pulling you from obedience, or pushing you toward what is unlawful. Don’t obey them in that. But don’t punish or give up on them: pardon, overlook and forgive, and Allah forgives. All wealth and children are a fitnah, a test.

So have taqwā as much as you can: do what you are able to. Listen, obey and spend; it is better for you. The real barrier is shuḥḥ, the stinginess built into the soul, and whoever is saved from it succeeds. Spending gladly for Allah is a loan He multiplies and rewards with forgiveness.
teaches: Love for family must never lead to disobeying Allah.
Be firm about Allah’s commands, yet gentle with your family.
Do your best; Allah asks only what you can bear.
Stinginess is the soul’s barrier to success.
Charity is a loan Allah repays many times over.
sections.hook: Ayah 14 says “among (min) your spouses and children”; ayah 15 drops min: “your wealth and your children,” the same pair as 63:9. The surah closes on five names of Allah.

groups.text: Everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Allah, who owns all, deserves all praise, and can do anything.
He created you; some became disbelievers and some believers, and He sees everything you do.
He created all with purpose, shaped you beautifully, and knows what you hide, what you show, and what is in hearts.
Past nations rejected their human messengers and tasted ruin, with worse to come. Allah had no need of them.
Deniers say there is no resurrection. Yes, by my Lord, you will be raised. So believe in Allah, His Messenger and the Qur’an.
On the Day of loss and gain, believers enter gardens forever and deniers enter the Fire forever.
No hardship strikes except by Allah’s leave, and whoever believes, Allah guides his heart.
Obey Allah and His Messenger, whose duty is only to convey. There is no god but Allah, so rely on Him.
Some spouses and children hold you back from Allah: beware, yet forgive. Wealth and children are a test.
Fear Allah as much as you can, obey and spend. A goodly loan to Allah is multiplied, and He forgives.

1.explain: Yusabbiḥu: everything declares Allah free of every flaw. Al-mulk: all control is His. Al-ḥamd: He is praised for His qualities, His creation, His laws and His blessings. Whatever He wills happens.

2.explain: Either He created people as believers and disbelievers by His decree, or created them and they then chose. Their choice is real and within His decree. He is baṣīr: He sees every deed and will repay it.

3.explain: Bil-ḥaqq: with wisdom and purpose, not in play. He shaped you in the finest form of any creature, no two faces alike. Al-maṣīr: you return to Him, to be repaid and asked about His blessings.

4.explain: He knows what is in the heavens and earth, what you hide and what you show, and dhāt aṣ-ṣudūr: every good intention and bad motive in the heart. So guard your inner self.

5.explain: Addressed to the disbelievers of Makkah: the news of earlier nations like ʿĀd and Thamūd. They tasted wabāl, the bad result of their deeds, in this world, and a painful punishment awaits in the Hereafter.

6.explain: Their messengers brought clear proofs, but they said, “Abasharun yahdūnanā?” Shall mere humans guide us? They turned away, and Allah had no need of their faith. He is ghanī, free of need, and ḥamīd.

7.explain: Zaʿama: to claim without proof. The Prophet ﷺ is told to swear by his Lord that they will be raised and told everything they did. Bringing back is easier than creating the first time.
7.why: Reportedly revealed about al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, a disbeliever of Makkah, in his dealings with Khabbāb. It then applied to everyone who denies the resurrection.

8.explain: Believe in Allah, His Messenger and an-nūr, the light, which is the Qur’an. It shines by itself and lights up what pleases Allah, His laws, and the realities of the Hereafter.

9.explain: Yawm al-jamʿ: all generations gathered in one place. At-taghābun: believers take the places in Paradise the disbelievers could have had. The disbeliever’s loss is total; even believers regret the good they missed.

10.explain: Those who disbelieved and denied Allah’s signs, despite clear proofs, are the people of the Fire forever. It is the worst destination, holding every hardship and misery.

11.explain: Muṣībah: any hardship in body, wealth or family. It comes only by Allah’s idhn, His decree. Believe that, and He guides your heart to patience and calm: what hit you was never going to miss you.
11.why: Reportedly the disbelievers said, “If the Muslims were right, Allah would have protected them from hardship.” This ayah replied that every hardship comes by Allah’s knowledge and decree.

12.explain: Obey Allah and His Messenger in every command and prohibition. If you turn away, the Messenger has done his part: al-balāgh al-mubīn, clear delivery. The message is from Allah; accepting it is up to us.

13.explain: Lā ilāha illā huwa: only Allah deserves worship. Tawakkul: rely on Him in every matter, trusting Him to take care of it. The stronger the faith, the stronger the trust.

14.explain: ʿAduww: an enemy by action, when family pulls you away from obeying Allah. Beware of obeying them in that. But pardon (taʿfū), overlook (taṣfaḥū) and forgive (taghfirū): don’t punish or give up on them.
14.why: Reportedly about men in Makkah whose wives and children stopped them emigrating to the Prophet ﷺ. When they arrived and saw how others had learned the religion, they wanted to punish their families. Another report names ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Ashjaʿī.

15.explain: Fitnah: a test, and a distraction from the Hereafter. The Prophet ﷺ once came down from the pulpit to pick up his two young grandsons, who were stumbling, and recited these words.

16.explain: Taqwā as much as you can: do what you are able to, and avoid what is forbidden. Shuḥḥ an-nafs: the stinginess built into the soul. Whoever is saved from it is truly successful.
16.why: Reportedly, when 3:102 (“fear Allah as He should be feared”) came, it was very hard on the Companions, and this ayah eased it. Another view links it to emigration: don’t let wealth or children keep you from it.

17.explain: Qarḍ ḥasan: spending lawful wealth gladly for Allah’s sake. He multiplies it, ten to seven hundred times and more, and forgives sins through it. Shakūr: gives much for little. Ḥalīm: doesn’t rush to punish.

18.explain: He knows al-ghayb, the unseen, and ash-shahādah, the seen. Al-ʿAzīz: no one can overpower Him. Al-Ḥakīm: He puts everything in its right place, in creation and in command.
